title.narrative: Response to Conflict Affected Households in Somalia-Galdogob District, Mudug Region.

description.narrative: Resource-based conflicts are a recurring phenomenon in many locations of Somalia. In the face of a weak governance system, competition among clan groups (or between clan groups and the authorities) over access to and control of resources leads to conflict and sometimes to violence. Considering that climatic shocks (e.g drought, floods etc.) are increasing in severity, magnitude and frequency and Somalia’s predominant agropastoral dependent livelihoods, conflict over pasture and water is increasingly becoming common. The scarcity of natural resources has fostered rivalries due to inequalities and the marginalization of some clans. This situation is exacerbated by reduced funding levels coinciding with the drawdown of ATMIS and increased complexity in conflict dynamics. Conflict and insecurity are high risks which are anticipated to generate above-average humanitarian impact during the last quarter of 2024. This, coupled with the bleak La Nina predictions will erode the food security gains so far achieved. The situation remains dynamic and unpredictable in FAO’s operational areas primarily geared towards stemming the conflict-induced displacement at the origin mostly in rural, peri urban and hard to reach areas. Galdogob experienced a wave of conflict leading to displacement of households and severe disruption of livelihoods. This has worsened an already dire situation for most of the population that are predominantly agropastoral. Abrupt displacement does not prepare families to salvage their assets, many leave to scamper for safety with family separation inevitable. Through this funding 2,550 households (15300 individuals) affected by conflict will be able to purchase their most critical needs including food and water. In addition, this funding will enable households settle within the host community as opposed to moving to camps for the internal person.
